questions.stem: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3:2. If 20 liters of this mixture is replaced with water, the ratio becomes 3:7. What is the original quantity of the mixture?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Replacement Problem with Ratio Change - Initial Ratio: Milk:Water = 3:2 - Let original quantity = 5x liters (milk = 3x, water = 2x) - After replacing 20 liters with water: - Milk removed = 20 × (3/5) = 12 liters - Water removed = 20 × (2/5) = 8 liters - Milk left = 3x - 12, Water left = 2x - 8 + 20 = 2x + 12 - New ratio: (3x - 12):(2x + 12) = 3:7 - Cross multiply: 7(3x - 12) = 3(2x + 12) - 21x - 84 = 6x + 36 ⟹ 15x = 120 ⟹ x = 8 - Original quantity = 5x = 40 liters

questions.stem: Tea of two types costing Rs. 300 per kg and Rs. 400 per kg are mixed in the ratio 2:3. What is the cost price of the mixture per kg?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Cost - Two Component Mixture - Alligation Formula: Cost = (Q₁×C₁ + Q₂×C₂)/(Q₁+Q₂) - Given: Q₁:Q₂ = 2:3, C₁ = Rs. 300, C₂ = Rs. 400 - Calculation: Cost = (2×300 + 3×400)/(2+3) = (600 + 1200)/5 = 1800/5 = Rs. 360 ✓

questions.stem: In a mixture of 40 liters, the ratio of acid and water is 1:3. How much acid should be added to make it 1:2?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Adding Component to Change Ratio - Initial: Acid:Water = 1:3 in 40 liters - Acid = 10 liters, Water = 30 liters - Required ratio: 1:2 - If acid = x, then water:acid = 2:1 - So 30/(10+x) = 2/1 ⟹ 30 = 2(10+x) - 30 = 20 + 2x ⟹ x = 5 liters - Alternative: Let acid added = y - New ratio: (10+y):30 = 1:2 ⟹ 2(10+y) = 30 - 20 + 2y = 30 ⟹ y = 5… wait, answer is 4 - Recalculation: (10+y)/30 = 1/2 ⟹ 2(10+y) = 30 ⟹ 10+y = 15 ⟹ y = 5

questions.stem: A merchant has 100 kg of sugar. He sells a part of it at 10% profit and the rest at 20% profit. If his overall profit is 14%, then what is the quantity sold at 20% profit?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Alligation for Profit Distribution - Method: Using alligation for weighted average profit - Setup: Profit₁ = 10%, Profit₂ = 20%, Average Profit = 14% - Using alligation cross method: - Distance from 10% to 14% = 4 - Distance from 14% to 20% = 6 - Ratio of quantities: Q₁:Q₂ = 6:4 = 3:2 - If total = 100 kg, then Q₂ = (2/5) × 100 = 40 kg ✓

questions.stem: Two solutions have salt concentrations of 8% and 12% respectively. In what ratio should they be mixed to get a solution of 10% concentration?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Alligation for Concentration Mixing - Given: Concentration₁ = 8%, Concentration₂ = 12%, Target = 10% - Using alligation cross method: - 8% ——— (12-10)=2 - 10% (mean) - 12% ——— (10-8)=2 - Wait, this gives 1:1

questions.stem: A vessel initially contains 60 liters of pure milk. 10 liters of milk is drawn out and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more. What is the amount of pure milk left in the vessel?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Repeated Replacement Problem - Formula: Final quantity = Initial × (1 - fraction_removed)^n - Given: Initial milk = 60 liters, Each time 10 liters drawn and replaced with water - Fraction replaced each time = 10/60 = 1/6 - Fraction remaining = 5/6 - After first replacement: 60 × (5/6) = 50 liters - After second replacement: 50 × (5/6) = 41.67 liters - Verification: Using formula: 60 × (5/6)² = 60 × 25/36 = 41.67 liters - Per answer: 43.50 liters (Might use different calculation method)

questions.stem: A mixture contains three types of rice in the ratio 2:3:5. If the three types cost Rs. 20, Rs. 30, and Rs. 40 per kg respectively, what is the average cost of the mixture per kg?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Cost - Three Component Mixture - Given: Ratio = 2:3:5, Costs = Rs. 20, Rs. 30, Rs. 40 per kg - Total parts = 2+3+5 = 10 - Average cost = (2×20 + 3×30 + 5×40)/10 = (40 + 90 + 200)/10 = 330/10 = Rs. 33

questions.stem: Two types of flour costing Rs. 15 per kg and Rs. 25 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3:2. What is the cost of the mixture per kg?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Cost - Two Component Mixture - Given: Ratio = 3:2, Costs = Rs. 15, Rs. 25 per kg - Average cost = (3×15 + 2×25)/(3+2) = (45 + 50)/5 = 95/5 = Rs. 19 ✓

questions.stem: A mixture of 90 liters contains milk and water in the ratio 2:1. How much water should be added to make the ratio 1:2?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Adding Component to Change Ratio - Initial: Milk:Water = 2:1 in 90 liters - Milk = 60 liters, Water = 30 liters - Target ratio: 1:2 (Water double the milk) - If water = W, then milk:water = 1:2 - 60:W = 1:2 ⟹ W = 120 liters - Water to add = 120 - 30 = 90 liters… but answer is 60 - Recalculation: 60/(30+x) = 1/2 ⟹ 2×60 = 30+x ⟹ x = 90 liters… option shows 60 - Verify with option C: Adding 60 liters: Ratio = 60:90 = 2:3 (not 1:2)**

questions.stem: Three types of nuts costing Rs. 50, Rs. 60, and Rs. 80 per kg are mixed in the ratio 3:4:2. What is the cost price of the mixture per kg?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Cost - Three Component Mixture - Given: Ratio = 3:4:2, Costs = Rs. 50, Rs. 60, Rs. 80 - Total parts = 3+4+2 = 9 - Average cost = (3×50 + 4×60 + 2×80)/9 = (150 + 240 + 160)/9 = 550/9 = Rs. 61.11

questions.stem: A vessel contains 100 liters of a mixture with milk and water in 7:3 ratio. If 20 liters of the mixture is replaced with milk, what is the new ratio of milk to water?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Replacement Problem with Single Component Addition - Initial: Milk:Water = 7:3 in 100 liters - Milk = 70 liters, Water = 30 liters - After replacing 20 liters mixture with milk: - Milk removed = 20 × (7/10) = 14 liters - Water removed = 20 × (3/10) = 6 liters - Milk added = 20 liters - Final: Milk = 70 - 14 + 20 = 76 liters, Water = 30 - 6 = 24 liters - New ratio = 76:24 = 19:6

questions.stem: A merchant mixes sugar costing Rs. 18 per kg with sugar costing Rs. 24 per kg. If he wants to sell the mixture at Rs. 20 per kg without any profit or loss, in what ratio should he mix them?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Alligation for No Profit/Loss Mixing - Given: Cost₁ = Rs. 18, Cost₂ = Rs. 24, Selling Price = Rs. 20 - For no profit/loss, selling price = average cost = 20 - Using alligation: 18 ——— (20-18)=2 - 20 (mean) - 24 ——— (24-20)=4 - Ratio = 4:2 = 2:1 ✓

questions.stem: A liquid mixture has alcohol and water in the ratio 5:3. If 8 liters of water is added, the ratio becomes 5:5. What is the original quantity of alcohol in the mixture?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Adding Component to Change Ratio - Initial: Alcohol:Water = 5:3 - Let Alcohol = 5x, Water = 3x - After adding 8 liters water: Alcohol:Water = 5:5 (= 1:1) - 5x:(3x+8) = 1:1 ⟹ 5x = 3x + 8 - 2x = 8 ⟹ x = 4 - Original alcohol = 5×4 = 20 liters ✓

questions.stem: Two types of coffee costing Rs. 80 per kg and Rs. 120 per kg are mixed in the ratio 1:2. What is the average cost per kg?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Cost - Two Component Mixture - Given: Ratio = 1:2, Costs = Rs. 80, Rs. 120 per kg - Average cost = (1×80 + 2×120)/(1+2) = (80 + 240)/3 = 320/3 = Rs. 106.67 ✓

questions.stem: A mixture contains acid and water in the ratio 1:4. 5 liters of acid is added, and the ratio becomes 1:3. What was the original quantity of the mixture?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Adding Single Component to Change Ratio - Initial: Acid:Water = 1:4 - Let Acid = x, Water = 4x - After adding 5 liters acid: Acid:Water = 1:3 - (x+5):4x = 1:3 ⟹ 3(x+5) = 4x - 3x + 15 = 4x ⟹ x = 15 - Original quantity = x + 4x = 5x = 5×5 = 25 liters ✓

questions.stem: A merchant has 600 kg of rice. He sells 40% of it at a profit of 15% and the rest at a profit of 10%. What is his overall profit percentage?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Alligation for Profit Distribution - Given: 40% sold at 15% profit, 60% sold at 10% profit - Overall profit = 0.4×15 + 0.6×10 = 6 + 6 = 12% ✓

questions.stem: Two types of oil with prices Rs. 100 per liter and Rs. 150 per liter are mixed. If the cost of the mixture is Rs. 130 per liter, in what ratio are they mixed?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Alligation for Price Mixing - Given: Price₁ = Rs. 100, Price₂ = Rs. 150, Average = Rs. 130 - Using alligation cross method: - 100 ——— (150-130)=20 - 130 (mean) - 150 ——— (130-100)=30 - Ratio = 30:20 = 3:2

questions.stem: A mixture of milk and water in a container has milk 75% by weight. If 50 kg of this mixture is withdrawn and replaced with 50 kg of water, the percentage of milk becomes 60%. What was the original quantity?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Replacement Problem with Percentage Change - Initial: Milk = 75% ⟹ Water = 25% - After replacing 50 kg with water: Milk % = 60% - Let original quantity = Q - Original milk = 0.75Q - Milk removed = 50 × 0.75 = 37.5 kg - Final milk = 0.75Q - 37.5 - New percentage: (0.75Q - 37.5)/Q = 0.60 - 0.75Q - 37.5 = 0.60Q ⟹ 0.15Q = 37.5 ⟹ Q = 250 kg

questions.stem: A liquid contains 80% acid. If 10 liters of this acid is mixed with 5 liters of water, what is the percentage of acid in the new mixture?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Concentration Calculation in Mixture - Initial: 80% acid in 10 liters = 8 liters acid - After adding 5 liters water: Total = 15 liters with 8 liters acid - New concentration = 8/15 × 100 = 53.33% ✓

questions.stem: A container has 120 liters of milk. 30 liters of milk is withdrawn and the same quantity of water is added. This process is repeated twice. What is the final quantity of milk in the container?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Repeated Replacement Problem - Formula: Final = Initial × (1 - fraction_removed)^n - Given: Initial = 120 liters, Each time 30 liters drawn (fraction = 1/4) - After 1st replacement: 120 × (3/4) = 90 liters - After 2nd replacement: 90 × (3/4) = 67.5 liters - Using formula: 120 × (3/4)² = 120 × 9/16 = 67.5 liters** ✓

questions.stem: Three solutions with 10%, 20%, and 30% concentration are mixed in the ratio 3:2:1. What is the concentration of the final mixture?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Weighted Average Concentration - Three Components - Given: Concentrations = 10%, 20%, 30%, Ratio = 3:2:1 - Total parts = 3+2+1 = 6 - Average concentration = (3×10 + 2×20 + 1×30)/6 = (30 + 40 + 30)/6 = 100/6 = 16.67% ✓

questions.stem: A merchant has 800 kg of tea. He mixes it with another type of tea in the ratio 4:1. If the first tea costs Rs. 400 per kg and the mixture costs Rs. 420 per kg on average, what is the cost per kg of the second type of tea?
questions.keySolution: Subtopic: Finding Cost of Unknown Component in Mixture - Given: Ratio = 4:1, First tea cost = Rs. 400, Mixture average = Rs. 420 - Using weighted average: (4×400 + 1×C₂)/5 = 420 - 1600 + C₂ = 2100 ⟹ C₂ = Rs. 500
